name: Jensen Huang
title: From Toilet Duty to Five Trillion
subtitle: How a boy from a Kentucky reform school and a Denny's kitchen built Nvidia, the chip company that powers AI, and what he got right and wrong along the way.
hook: In the mid-1970s, a ==nine-year-old== Jensen Huang and his older brother were sent to live in the dormitory of Oneida Baptist Institute in rural Kentucky. His relatives thought it was a good boarding school. It was a reform academy, and the little boy's job was to __clean all the bathrooms__. Fifty years later he runs Nvidia, which in 2025 became worth ==more than $5 trillion==, and that same school now has a building named after him, paid for with a **$2 million** matching grant from Huang and his wife, Lori.

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Taiwan, then Thailand. Sent to the US at nine with his older brother, first to a reform academy in Kentucky, then reunited with his family in Oregon. Finished high school at 16 and was a nationally ranked junior table-tennis player.

glance.label: Education
glance.value: BS in electrical engineering, Oregon State University (1984); MS in electrical engineering, Stanford (1992), earned while working full time

glance.label: First job
glance.value: At 15, a Denny's restaurant in the Portland, Oregon area: dishwasher, then busboy, then waiter

glance.label: Before Nvidia
glance.value: Chip designer at AMD (1984–85), then eight years at LSI Logic (1985–93)

glance.label: First company (age)
glance.value: Nvidia, co-founded in 1993 at 30 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, planned in a Denny's booth in San Jose

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: Nvidia: president and CEO since day one. About 42,000 employees in 38 countries; market value passed $5 trillion in 2025

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: About 4% of Nvidia. Forbes real-time net worth $186.6 billion, No. 7 in the world (29 Oct 2026)

glance.label: Family
glance.value: Married to Lori Huang (née Mills), his lab partner in a first-year engineering class at Oregon State; two adult children, Spencer and Madison

contact.howToReach: Huang has no personal X or Instagram account that we could find; his one personal social account is a LinkedIn profile with about 2 million followers, so a cold message there is very unlikely to be read. If you are building an AI startup, the real door into his world is NVIDIA Inception: it is free, takes companies under 10 years old at any stage with no revenue needed, and includes networking events with investors and Nvidia executives. Journalists should use press@nvidia.com (or india-pr@nvidia.com in India), investors should use the Investor Relations form or (877) 7-NVIDIA, and job seekers should go through the careers site, not the CEO. Never email guessed addresses, pay a "contact finder" site, or trust anyone online who claims to be Huang and asks for money or crypto. Whatever channel you use, keep it under 150 words: who you are, what you have actually built with Nvidia technology, and one clear ask.

factCheck.method: Front matter and contact card built from primary records first: Nvidia's FY2026 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 25 Feb 2026), Nvidia's own contact, newsroom, investor-relations and Inception pages, and Huang's official company biography. Childhood and education facts were cross-checked against Oneida Baptist Institute's own page on Jen-Hsun Huang Hall, Oregon State University's Engineering Hall of Fame entry and newsroom, the Carnegie Corporation's Great Immigrants profile and the Computer History Museum. Press details come from Fortune, NBC Bay Area and CBS 60 Minutes. Net worth and ownership are the Forbes real-time figures read on 29 Oct 2026. Photos and licences were read from the Wikimedia Commons API (imageinfo/extmetadata); thumbnails use 960px because Commons rejects a 1000px width. Socials cite Nvidia's own website footers or the profile itself; no personal phones, guessed emails or data-broker sites were used. Several outlets (Britannica, New Yorker, Business Insider, NYT, Bloomberg, CNBC) blocked our fetcher, so we did not cite them.

disputed.note: The Computer History Museum says Tainan, Taiwan; Wikipedia gives Taipei, citing Stephen Witt's 2025 book. We use Tainan.
17 February 1963 is widely reported, and Nvidia's Feb 2026 10-K lists him as 63, which fits. We could not read a primary source giving the day, so the glance gives the year only.

disputed.claim: Huang's age at Oneida Baptist Institute
disputed.note: The school's own page says he was nine; the Carnegie Corporation says he was sent to an uncle at nine and enrolled at Oneida at ten. We say nine, and the chapters may say 'nine or ten'.

Fortune, citing an Nvidia blog post, says a Denny's in the Portland, Oregon area at 15. NBC Bay Area's report from the San Jose plaque event suggests he worked at that San Jose branch. He grew up in Oregon, so we go with the Portland area; the San Jose Denny's on Berryessa Road is where Nvidia was planned.

disputed.claim: Year Jensen and Lori Huang married
disputed.note: Oregon State says they met as freshman lab partners and married five years later; 1985 is often given but we found no primary source, so we leave the year out.
Nvidia publishes it as the vanity number (877) 7-NVIDIA; the dial link spells it out as +1 877 768 4342 using standard keypad letters.
